problems.description: Design a data structure that supports adding new words and searching for a string, where the search can use '.' as a wildcard that matches any single letter. Implement addWord and search methods. All words consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.input: addWord("bad"), addWord("dad"), addWord("mad"), search("pad"), search("bad"), search(".ad"), search("b..")
examples.explanation: 'pad' was never added, 'bad' was added, '.ad' matches 'bad', 'dad', 'mad', and 'b..' matches 'bad'.

bruteForce.explanation: Store all words in a list and for each search pattern, check each word using character-by-character comparison treating '.' as matching any character.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n*m) per search where n is number of words and m is word length

optimal.explanation: Use a trie where search uses DFS/backtracking when encountering '.', exploring all 26 children, giving O(m) average and O(26^m) worst case for all wildcards.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(m) average, O(26^m) worst case with all wildcards

problems.title: Word Search II Trie
problems.description: Given an m x n board of characters and a list of words, return all words on the board. Each word must be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically neighboring). The same cell may not be used more than once in a word.

examples.explanation: 'eat' can be found starting at board[1][3] going left, and 'oath' starting at board[3][0] going up then right.

bruteForce.explanation: For each word, do a DFS/backtracking on the board to check if it exists, resulting in O(words * m * n * 4^L) time where L is word length.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(W * m * n * 4^L) where W is number of words and L is max word length

optimal.explanation: Build a Trie from all words, then do a single DFS on the board guided by the Trie to prune paths early, reducing redundant searches across words.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(m * n * 4^L) for DFS plus O(W*L) to build trie

problems.title: Replace Words
problems.description: Given a dictionary of root words and a sentence, replace each word in the sentence with the shortest root from the dictionary that is a prefix of that word. If a word has no root, leave it unchanged. Return the modified sentence as a string.

examples.input: dictionary = ["cat","bat","rat"], sentence = "the cattle was rattled by the battery"
examples.output: "the cat was rat by the bat"
examples.explanation: 'cattle' starts with root 'cat', 'rattled' starts with root 'rat', 'battery' starts with root 'bat'.

bruteForce.explanation: For each word in the sentence, iterate through all dictionary roots and replace with the shortest one that is a prefix of the word.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(W * D * L) where W is words in sentence, D is dictionary size, L is word length

optimal.explanation: Build a Trie from dictionary roots, then for each sentence word traverse the Trie to find the shortest matching root in O(L) time per word.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(D*L + W*L) for building trie and processing sentence

problems.title: Map Sum Pairs
problems.description: Design a map that accepts a string key and an integer value, and supports a sum method returning the sum of all values whose keys start with a given prefix. If a key is inserted again, its value overwrites the original. Keys consist of lowercase letters.

examples.explanation: After inserting 'apple'=3, sum of keys starting with 'ap' is 3. After inserting 'app'=2, sum is 3+2=5.

bruteForce.explanation: Store key-value pairs in a hash map and for sum, iterate through all entries checking if each key starts with the given prefix.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n*m) per sum query where n is entries and m is key length

optimal.explanation: Use a Trie where each node stores the cumulative sum of all values passing through it, enabling O(m) sum queries by traversing to the prefix node.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(m) per insert and sum where m is key/prefix length
optimal.spaceComplexity: O(n*m) for trie plus O(n*m) for hashmap

problems.title: Longest Word in Dictionary
problems.description: Given an array of strings words, find the longest word that can be built one character at a time by other words in the array. If there are multiple answers, return the lexicographically smallest one. All words contain only lowercase letters.

examples.explanation: The word 'world' can be built: 'w' -> 'wo' -> 'wor' -> 'word' -> 'world', each being a word in the array.

bruteForce.explanation: Sort the words, use a set to track buildable words, and for each word check if its prefix (word minus last char) is in the set.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n*m*log(n)) where n is number of words and m is max word length

optimal.explanation: Build a Trie from all words, then BFS/DFS from root visiting only nodes marked as word ends, tracking the longest path found.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(n*m) to build trie and O(n*m) to traverse

problems.title: Short Encoding of Words
problems.description: Given a list of words, encode them using a reference string S and indices. Each word must appear as a suffix of S. Return the minimum length of S, where each word is appended with '#'. Duplicate words and words that are suffixes of others can be omitted.

examples.explanation: S = 'time#bell#' has length 10. 'time' starts at index 0, 'bell' at index 5, and 'me' is a suffix of 'time' so it's covered.

bruteForce.explanation: Remove any word that is a suffix of another word in the list, then sum the lengths of remaining words plus 1 for each '#' separator.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n * m^2) where n is number of words and m is max word length

optimal.explanation: Build a Trie using reversed words; leaf nodes (no children) represent words that cannot be encoded as suffixes of others, count their lengths plus 1.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(n*m) where n is number of words and m is max word length

problems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, return the maximum result of nums[i] XOR nums[j] where 0 <= i <= j < n. The array contains non-negative integers and n can be up to 2*10^4, with values up to 2^31.

examples.explanation: The maximum XOR is achieved with 5 XOR 25 = 28.

bruteForce.explanation: Try all pairs (i, j) and compute XOR for each pair, keeping track of the maximum value found.

optimal.explanation: Build a binary Trie of all numbers bit by bit from MSB; for each number, greedily traverse the Trie choosing the opposite bit to maximize XOR.

problems.title: Single Number
problems.description: Given a non-empty array of integers where every element appears twice except for one, find that single one. The algorithm must have O(n) time complexity and O(1) space complexity.

examples.explanation: Every number except 4 appears twice. XOR of all elements cancels out pairs, leaving 4.

bruteForce.explanation: Use a hash map to count occurrences of each number and return the one with count equal to 1.

optimal.explanation: XOR all numbers together: since a XOR a = 0 and a XOR 0 = a, all duplicate pairs cancel out leaving only the single number.

problems.title: Single Number II
problems.description: Given an integer array where every element appears exactly three times except for one element which appears exactly once, find the single element. The solution must use O(1) space.

examples.explanation: 2 appears 3 times, 3 appears once. The single number is 3.

bruteForce.explanation: Use a hash map to count occurrences and return the number with count not divisible by 3 (i.e., count == 1).

optimal.explanation: Use two bitmasks 'ones' and 'twos' to track bits that have appeared once and twice modulo 3; after processing all numbers, 'ones' holds the single number.

problems.title: Single Number III
problems.description: Given an integer array where exactly two elements appear only once and all other elements appear exactly twice, find the two elements that appear only once. Return them in any order using O(1) space.

examples.explanation: 3 and 5 each appear once, all others appear twice. XOR of all gives 3 XOR 5 = 6, then split by differing bit.

bruteForce.explanation: Use a hash map to count occurrences of each number, then collect all numbers with count equal to 1.

optimal.explanation: XOR all to get xor of the two singles, find a set bit to split numbers into two groups, XOR each group separately to isolate each single number.

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits
problems.description: Write a function that takes the binary representation of a positive integer and returns the number of set bits (also known as the Hamming weight). The input is a 32-bit unsigned integer.

examples.explanation: The binary representation has three '1' bits.

bruteForce.explanation: Repeatedly check the least significant bit by ANDing with 1, count if set, then right-shift until the number becomes 0.

optimal.explanation: Use Brian Kernighan's algorithm: n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit each iteration, so the loop runs exactly as many times as there are set bits.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(k) where k is number of set bits

problems.title: Reverse Bits
problems.description: Reverse the bits of a given 32-bit unsigned integer and return the result. For example, if the input is 00000010100101000001111010011100, reverse all 32 bits to get 00111001011110000010100101000000.

examples.explanation: The 32-bit binary representation is reversed bit by bit.

bruteForce.explanation: Extract each bit from the input using right shifts, and place it in the reversed position in the result using left shifts, iterating all 32 bit positions.

optimal.explanation: Use divide-and-conquer bit swapping with masks: swap adjacent bits, then pairs, then nibbles, then bytes, and finally 16-bit halves in O(1) operations.

problems.title: Missing Number XOR Approach
problems.description: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], find the one missing number in that range. Solve using the XOR bit manipulation approach with O(1) extra space.

examples.explanation: n = 3 so the range is [0,3]. 2 is the missing number. XOR of [0,1,2,3] XOR [3,0,1] = 2.

bruteForce.explanation: Compute the expected sum of [0..n] using the formula n*(n+1)/2, subtract the actual sum of the array to find the missing number.

optimal.explanation: XOR all indices 0..n with all array values; duplicate XORs cancel out leaving only the missing number, handling potential overflow issues with sum.

problems.title: Hamming Distance
problems.description: The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of positions at which the corresponding bits differ. Given two integers x and y, return their Hamming distance. Both integers are non-negative and less than 2^31.

examples.explanation: 1 = 0001, 4 = 0100. They differ in 2 bit positions, so Hamming distance is 2.

bruteForce.explanation: XOR the two numbers to get bits that differ, then count the number of set bits in the result by checking each bit position.

optimal.explanation: XOR the two numbers, then use Brian Kernighan's bit trick (n &= n-1) to count set bits efficiently by clearing the lowest set bit each iteration.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(k) where k is number of differing bits

problems.title: Power of Two
problems.description: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two, otherwise return false. An integer n is a power of two if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x. The input can be negative or zero.

examples.explanation: 16 = 2^4, so it is a power of two.

bruteForce.explanation: Repeatedly divide n by 2 while it's even and greater than 1; if we reach exactly 1, it's a power of two.

optimal.explanation: A power of two has exactly one set bit; use the trick n > 0 && (n & (n-1)) == 0 which clears the only set bit, resulting in 0 for powers of two.

problems.title: Power of Three
problems.description: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of three, otherwise return false. An integer n is a power of three if there exists an integer x such that n == 3^x. Try to solve it without using a loop or recursion.

examples.explanation: 27 = 3^3, so it is a power of three.

bruteForce.explanation: Repeatedly divide n by 3 while it's divisible by 3 and greater than 1; if we reach exactly 1, it's a power of three.

optimal.explanation: The largest power of 3 fitting in a 32-bit int is 3^19 = 1162261467; if n > 0 and 1162261467 % n == 0, then n is a power of three.

problems.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
problems.description: Given two integers left and right that represent a range [left, right], return the bitwise AND of all numbers in that range, inclusive. The inputs are non-negative integers up to 2^31 - 1.

examples.explanation: 5 & 6 & 7 = 4. The common prefix of 5(101), 6(110), 7(111) in binary is 1, so result is 100 = 4.

bruteForce.explanation: Iterate through all numbers from left to right computing the AND of all of them, stopping early if the result becomes 0.

optimal.explanation: Find the common prefix of left and right in binary by right-shifting both until they are equal; the result is this common prefix shifted back left.
optimal.timeComplexity: O(log n) where n is the maximum value

problems.title: Sum of Two Integers without Arithmetic Operators
problems.description: Given two integers a and b, return the sum of the two integers without using the operators + and -. Use bit manipulation to simulate the addition process. Both a and b fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

examples.explanation: 1 + 2 = 3. XOR gives sum without carry (1^2=3), AND shifted gives carry (1&2=0 so no carry needed here).

bruteForce.explanation: Use Python-style iteration: XOR gives sum without carry, AND shifted left gives carry; repeat until no carry remains.

optimal.explanation: Use recursion: base case when b is 0 return a; otherwise return getSum(a XOR b, (a AND b) << 1) to propagate carry bits.

problems.title: Divide Two Integers
problems.description: Given two integers dividend and divisor, divide without using multiplication, division, or mod operators. Return the quotient truncated toward zero. Assume the environment can only store 32-bit signed integers in range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1].

examples.explanation: 10 / 3 = 3.33..., truncated to 3.

bruteForce.explanation: Repeatedly subtract the divisor from the dividend and count how many times until the dividend is less than the divisor, but this is too slow for large inputs.

optimal.explanation: Use bit shifting to double the divisor exponentially, finding the largest multiple at each step, reducing the dividend quickly in O(log^2 n) time.

problems.title: Repeated DNA Sequences
problems.description: The DNA sequence is composed of the letters 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T'. Given a string s representing a DNA sequence, return all 10-letter-long sequences that occur more than once in the string. The answer may be in any order.

examples.explanation: Both 10-letter sequences appear more than once in the string.

bruteForce.explanation: Use a hash map of strings, extract every 10-character substring and track those seen more than once.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n * 10) = O(n) but with high string hashing constant

optimal.explanation: Encode each character as 2 bits (A=0,C=1,G=2,T=3), use a rolling 20-bit integer hash for each 10-char window, store in integer hash set for O(1) lookup.

problems.title: Gray Code
problems.description: An n-bit Gray code sequence is a sequence of 2^n integers where every pair of adjacent values differs in exactly one bit, the first and last values also differ in exactly one bit, and all 2^n integers are used exactly once. Given n, return any valid Gray code sequence.

examples.explanation: 0=00, 1=01, 3=11, 2=10. Each adjacent pair differs in exactly one bit, and wrapping around 2(10)->0(00) also differs by one bit.

bruteForce.explanation: Use BFS/backtracking to build the sequence by exploring numbers differing in one bit from the current, tracking visited numbers.

optimal.explanation: Use the formula: Gray code of i is i XOR (i >> 1). This directly generates the standard reflected binary Gray code for all i from 0 to 2^n - 1.

problems.title: Total Hamming Distance
problems.description: The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of positions where their bits differ. Given an integer array nums, return the sum of Hamming distances between all pairs of integers. The array can have up to 10^4 elements with values up to 10^9.

examples.explanation: Hamming(4,14)=2, Hamming(4,2)=2, Hamming(14,2)=2. Total = 2+2+2 = 6.

bruteForce.explanation: Compute pairwise Hamming distance for all pairs using XOR and popcount, summing them all up in O(n^2) time.

optimal.explanation: For each bit position, count how many numbers have that bit set (k) and how many don't (n-k); pairs contributing to Hamming distance = k*(n-k). Sum over all 32 bit positions.

problems.title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
problems.description: Given an integer num, return the number of steps to reduce it to zero. In one step, if num is even divide it by 2, otherwise subtract 1 from it. The input num is a non-negative integer up to 10^6.

examples.explanation: 14 -> 7 (div 2) -> 6 (sub 1) -> 3 (div 2) -> 2 (sub 1) -> 1 (div 2) -> 0 (sub 1). That's 6 steps.

bruteForce.explanation: Simulate the process directly: repeatedly check if num is even or odd, apply the corresponding operation, and count steps until num reaches zero.

optimal.explanation: Count bits: each 0-bit requires 1 step (right shift), each 1-bit requires 2 steps (subtract then shift), except the leading 1-bit needs only 1 step. Total = bits + set_bits - 1.

problems.title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
problems.description: Given an array arr and a 2D array queries where queries[i] = [left, right], return an array of answers where answer[i] is the XOR of all elements in arr[left..right] inclusive. There are up to 3*10^4 queries and arr has up to 3*10^4 elements.

bruteForce.explanation: For each query [left, right], XOR all elements from index left to right individually.
bruteForce.timeComplexity: O(n * q) where n is arr length and q is number of queries

optimal.explanation: Build a prefix XOR array where prefix[i] = XOR of arr[0..i-1]; then XOR of arr[l..r] = prefix[r+1] XOR prefix[l], answering each query in O(1).
optimal.timeComplexity: O(n + q) where n is arr length and q is number of queries

problems.title: Find the Difference
problems.description: You are given two strings s and t where t is generated by random shuffling of s and then adding one more random character at a random position. Find and return the character that was added to t. Both strings contain only lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: 'e' is the extra character added to t. XOR of all characters in s and t cancels duplicates, leaving 'e'.

bruteForce.explanation: Count character frequencies using a hash map for s, subtract frequencies for t, and return the character with a non-zero (positive) remaining count in t.

optimal.explanation: XOR all characters in both s and t; since every character in s appears in t (and vice versa) except the extra one, XOR cancels paired characters leaving only the extra.

problems.title: Counting Bits
problems.description: Given an integer n, return an array ans of length n+1 where ans[i] is the number of 1s in the binary representation of i. Your algorithm should run in O(n) time and O(n) space.

examples.explanation: 0->0 bits, 1->1 bit, 2->1 bit, 3->2 bits, 4->1 bit, 5->2 bits.

bruteForce.explanation: For each number from 0 to n, count its set bits using bit shifting or __builtin_popcount, and store in the result array.

optimal.explanation: Use DP: ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1). The number of set bits in i equals the set bits in i/2 plus whether i is odd, building results from previously computed values.
